title: Add and Subtract Polynomials
student_objective: I can add and subtract polynomial expressions of degree one and two and write results in standard form.
teacher_objective: Diagnose like-term, coefficient, subtraction distribution, missing-term, exponent, standard-form, cancellation, and equivalence-check errors.

concept_cards.title: Match like terms
concept_cards.content: Like terms have exactly the same variable part and exponent. Only their coefficients combine.

concept_cards.title: Add by degree
concept_cards.content: Align quadratic terms, linear terms, and constants, then add coefficients within each group.

concept_cards.title: Distribute subtraction
concept_cards.content: When subtracting a polynomial, change the sign of every term in the polynomial before combining like terms.

concept_cards.title: Use zero placeholders
concept_cards.content: A missing degree has coefficient zero. Placeholders help keep terms aligned without changing the expression.

concept_cards.title: Write and verify standard form
concept_cards.content: Order terms from greatest exponent to least. Substitute a simple x-value into the original and result to check equivalence.

Pause after distributing subtraction to inspect every sign.

solution_steps.explanation: Represent the missing linear term with coefficient zero.
Reorder the second polynomial by degree.

items.prompt: A student says (5x²+3x)-(2x²-4x)=3x²-x. Is the result correct?
items.explanation_prompt: Explain the sign error and give the correct result.
items.explanation_guidance: Subtracting the second polynomial changes -4x to +4x. Thus 5x²+3x-2x²+4x=3x²+7x.
items.tutor_behavior: Require both the corrected sign and simplified expression.
Both variable parts are x².
Their exponents differ.
Add signed coefficients.
The missing linear terms contribute zero.
Subtract both 8x and 6.
Both the linear and constant terms cancel.
Order by descending exponent without changing signs.

items.prompt: What is the degree of the result when (2x²+x)+( -2x²+5x) is simplified?
items.tutor_behavior: The x² terms cancel, leaving 6x.

items.prompt: Can 2x²+3x be simplified to 5x³ by combining terms?
items.tutor_behavior: Addition does not add exponents, and unlike terms do not combine.

items.prompt: One area is 3x²+2x and another is x²-5x+6. Find their total area.
items.tutor_behavior: Add the area polynomials and retain square units if requested.

items.prompt: A revenue polynomial is 8x²+5x-2 and a cost polynomial is 3x²+7x+4. Find revenue minus cost.
items.tutor_behavior: Subtract every term of the cost polynomial.

items.prompt: At x=2, both an original polynomial sum and its simplified form equal 17. Does this single check prove they are equivalent for all x?
accepted_answers: no one value is not proof
items.tutor_behavior: A numerical check can catch errors but one input alone does not prove identity.

like_terms.teacher_signal: Combines terms with different variable parts or exponents

subtract_distribution.teacher_signal: Changes only the first sign when subtracting a polynomial

polynomial_subtraction.teacher_signal: Fails to distribute subtraction before combining

missing_terms.teacher_signal: Misaligns a polynomial with a missing degree

leading_term_cancellation.teacher_signal: Retains a canceled leading term or wrong degree

multiple_polynomials.teacher_signal: Loses signs across multiple grouping symbols

lower_term_cancellation.teacher_signal: Fails to remove zero linear or constant terms

standard_form.teacher_signal: Does not order by descending degree

degree_after_cancellation.teacher_signal: Uses the original degree after leading terms cancel

context_addition.teacher_signal: Does not translate total into polynomial addition

context_subtraction.teacher_signal: Does not translate difference into polynomial subtraction

equivalence_check.teacher_signal: Treats one numerical match as proof of identity
